acip: 'DOD NA, DON BYED NUS PA CHOS CAN, KHYOD MTSON BYA YIN KHYOD MTSON BYA DANG BDAG GCIG TU 'BREL, KHYOD MA YIN ZHING MTSON BYA YIN PA'I GZHI MTHUN PA DU MA GRUB PAR THAL, KHYOD MTSON BYA'I BYE BRAG YIN PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: 'dod na, don byed nus pa chos can, khyod mtshon bya yin khyod mtshon bya dang bdag gcig tu 'brel, khyod ma yin zhing mtshon bya yin pa'i gzhi mthun pa du ma grub par thal, khyod mtshon bya'i bye brag yin pa'i phyir
english: Yes, then I agree that the ability to perform a function is characteristic of a thing which is defined. Suppose you do agree. Let's consider then the ability to perform a function. Are you saying that it is (1) something to be defined; and that (2) it has a relationship to things to be defined such that to be it is to be something to be defined; and that (3) there are many examples of things which are not the ability to perform a function, but which are still things to be defined? Why do you say that? Because the ability to perform a function is characteristic of being something which is to be defined.
